definition: Psycholinguistics is the study of how people produce, receive, choose, and understand messages. It focuses on the mental and perceptual processes involved in turning thoughts into speech sounds and in interpreting those sounds back into meaning.

provenance.scope: Source record D011578; pinned source text

reasons: The phrasing about ‘turning thoughts into speech sounds’ and ‘interpreting those sounds back into meaning’ is more specific than the packet, which only says psycholinguistics concerns relations between messages and communicators and the processes of encoding and decoding.
‘Mental and perceptual processes’ is not stated in the packet and adds an unsupported generalization about the field.
The packet explicitly mentions individuals who “select and interpret” messages, but it does not explicitly support the definition’s inclusion of “produce, receive.”

The packet supports encoding/decoding in relation to messages and communicators (encoding via “phonetics” and decoding via “psychoacoustics”), but it does not directly support the specific framing that the process involves “turning thoughts into speech sounds.”
